control-performance-trust-installation.title: Untitled (Mirror)
control-performance-trust-installation.subtitle: Control, Performance & Trust
control-performance-trust-installation.summary: A responsive live-loop installation: a mirror that not only reflects the viewer but also tracks and visualizes their presence in real time. It overlays traces of previous observers, transforming the act of looking into both self-observation and the monitoring of others: Placing participants in the role of watcher and watched simultaneously. The installation materializes the research of the accompanying essay on surveillance as a form of preemptive control.
control-performance-trust-installation.outcome: A responsive live-loop mirror installation that reflects viewers while tracking and visualizing their presence in real time.

control-performance-trust-publication.subtitle: In Surveillance Society
control-performance-trust-publication.summary: Through a theory-informed practice, I developed a written essay shaped by continuous reflection on surveillance studies alongside iterative prototyping. The research was published as a bound essay and materialized in an accompanying interactive installation.

quantum-abacus.title: Quantum Abacus
quantum-abacus.summary: Quantum Abacus is a kinetic installation that translates superposition and probabilistic measurement into a physical, abacus-inspired exhibit. It was developed in a competition for the Institute of AI Saftey of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) in Collaboration with Parsons School of Design in New York. The project demonstrates a novel approach to science communication by allowing visitors to interact with quantum concepts directly. Instead of explaining quantum principles through abstraction alone, the project lets visitors manipulate probabilities and directly experience in real time how a calculation can be made, with the otherwise un-imaginable quantum mechanics. The project tested the boundaries of what is possible with typical science-communication approaches, as the principles of quantum computing are utterly incompatible with metaphors in the atomic scale world. As the winners of the competition, Cora Kindermann and me were employed by the DLR.
quantum-abacus.context: Winner of a Competition among collaborative, international teams to design an illustrative Science-communication exhibit of the DLR Institute of AI Safety

unwinding.title: Unwinding
unwinding.subtitle: A Quiet Place for Hong Kong
unwinding.summary: Unwinding is an exhibition pavilion concept developed during my exchange semester at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. It responds to the shrinking availability of freely accessible communal space in a dense, highly commercialized city where staying somewhere is usually tied to consumption. Inspired by the rhythm and atmosphere of a bamboo forest, the layered double-spiral structure creates a gradual transition from the open city into a calm, intimate core: visually and sonically sheltered, but never fully alienated from the bustle outside. Built entirely from bamboo using traditional Hong Kong scaffolding techniques, the pavilion is proposed as a place to pause, linger, and rest without purpose or purchase.

typecase.title: Typecase
typecase.summary: Typecase is a lightweight, native macOS utility designed for finding non-emoji Unicode characters using natural language. It comprehensively covers every Unicode character, even rendering invisible characters at their true width. For each character, the app can display code points in all common notations, shows how to type it using your keyboard, and allows for quick copying to the clipboard. Additionally, Typecase lists which installed fonts support the glyph, lets you open specific font files to browse all included characters, and features a floating Quick Lookup window that can be triggered via a shortcut to find and copy characters without ever leaving your active application.

aix-antiqua.title: Aix Antiqua
aix-antiqua.summary: Aix Antiqua is a modern variable redraw of a tall Garamond, made for my own personal use – you can see it all over this website. Just for fun, I added an ultra-slanted version.
aix-antiqua.context: I love Garamond, but all available digital versions have some shortcomings: they are either not variable, or similar fonts are already overused by AI tools right now.
aix-antiqua.approach:
Regular weight as the single reference master
Other weights generated by controlled stroke growth, keeping counters and letter shapes intact
Forward and reverse slants built by shearing each finished upright master
Kerning re-solved for every weight and slant, keeping the same real clearance as the regular
Masters interpolated into one variable font with weight and slant axes
aix-antiqua.outcome: Serif font with two variable axes: weight (300–600) and slant (−30° to +30°). Continuous upright, oblique and reverse-slant styles from one file, plus a separately drawn matching italic family. 377 glyphs covering 333 characters, with custom ligatures, stylistic alternates, full kerning and accent positioning.
aix-antiqua.result:
Variable Serif Font
Matching Italic Family
Webfont for milanelsen.com

tidal-exposures.title: Tidal Exposures
tidal-exposures.summary: Tidal Exposures is a series of analogue photographs developed in an experimental, home-made seaweed developer. Its scratches, stripes and softness would traditionally count as errors, but give the photos their characteristic look. Made during a workshop at the “Update” Media Art Festival in Liepāja, Latvia, in September 2025, which in that year had the theme of Baltic ecology under the title of “Blue Shift”.
